summary: Ran the molecular tests for M5-S03 (docs step, owner story-drafter, status was `built`). Zero XML files under the step's artefacts, recorded as ran-with-zero-files rather than skipped. The manifest check is skipped-not-applicable: the step's type is `docs` and its Output Contract and declared `outputs[]` produce a single markdown document (`story-backlog.md`), no `package.xml`. The one declared `checker` acceptance test, `check_invest.py --manifest-dir artefacts/M5-S03`, was run verbatim from the build directory and exited 0 (11/11 stories passed, 0 ERROR, 10 WARN on the 250-word heuristic, matching the plan's declared expectation), and `check-outputs` reported ok with no missing/empty/malformed paths. The one declared `manual` test names three observable outcomes and is deferred to the milestone gate, never counted as a failure. `results.json` records `passed: true` with an empty `failed[]`, and `set-status M5-S03 tested` succeeded.
confidence_rationale: Every declared test either ran to an observed exit code (checker: 0; check-outputs: ok) or was correctly classified (xml: ran-zero-files; manifest: skipped-not-applicable for a non-metadata docs step; manual: shape-checked and deferred). No command test was refused, no manifest exclusion for a coverage-gap type was needed, and check-outputs reported nothing missing, empty or malformed.

process_observations.observation: The step's declared checker command matches its own description exactly: `check_invest.py --manifest-dir artefacts/M5-S03` exited 0 with `Summary: 11/11 stories passed (0 ERROR, 10 WARN)`, the same figure the plan's acceptance-test description and the owning agent's envelope both predicted before this run.
check-outputs confirmed the step's single declared output exists, is non-empty and is not malformed, so `set-status tested` proceeded without a manual override.

All 10 WARNs on the checker are the same 250-word story-body heuristic, and three of the eleven stories (US-CASE-004, US-CASE-007, US-CASE-009) carry the heaviest overflow because their bodies embed the Q24 training note, the F-40 calendar-pin note and the completion-proxy note the M4 gate required. The checker has no way to separate 'story is too long' from 'story correctly carries a required handoff note', so every run of this checker on this backlog will show the same 10 WARNs until the notes are relocated out of the story body.

A `package.xml` exists under the dependency M5-S01's artefacts, but M5-S03 declares no package.xml and produces no metadata, so this run treated the manifest check as not-applicable to M5-S03 rather than checking story-backlog.md against M5-S01's manifest. standards/build-orchestration.md § 5's type-based branch ("docs that produces no manifest") supports this reading, but the § 5 step-1 text ("or under the artefacts of a step this one depends_on") does not explicitly say a found dependency manifest is irrelevant once the step's own type is in the non-metadata bucket — a human should confirm this reading holds for future non-metadata docs steps that depend on a metadata step.
M5-S03 is now `tested`; build-doc-keeper can compile the workbook, traceability and the M5-S04 UAT/acceptance-criteria pack from it.
process_observations.followup_reason: because M5-S04 depends_on M5-S03 and cannot enter `next` until M5-S03 is `documented`, which is build-doc-keeper's transition to make.

skipped_manual: Given Q77 and Q84, when story-backlog.md is read, then each of the three intake channels — email, web and manual UI — has its own story, every story names a tester persona holding the real profile plus permission set group (PSG_Tier1_Prod, PSG_Tier2_Prod, PSG_Billing_Prod) rather than the admin profile, and every story carries at least three Given/When/Then criteria including a permission-denial path (Q80).
